$comment: Plan of record from Gate 5 onward. Estimates are in VERIFICATION hours — the time to build it AND prove it, not the time to type it. The basis for each is stated, because an estimate without a basis is a wish.

stories.title: Schema migration with the no-double-booking constraint
stories.basis: The spike already proved the constraint. This is transcribing a proven design into a migration plus a rollback.
acceptance: 001_init.sql creates btree_gist, six tables, and the exclusion constraint from design/data-model.md
Every monetary column is integer and suffixed _paise
bookings has CHECK (upper(window_at) > lower(window_at)) and CHECK (amount_paise >= 0)
The migration runs on an empty database with no errors
A down migration exists and drops cleanly

stories.title: Indexes
stories.basis: Five indexes from a table already written in the data model.
acceptance: Indexes match the Keys and indexes table in design/data-model.md
The GiST index the exclusion constraint already creates is not duplicated

stories.title: Seed data: 7 areas, ~20 fictional spots, bays
stories.basis: Data entry with invented names. Slow only because coordinates must be plausible.
acceptance: Seven areas with Hyderabad coordinates
About twenty spots spread across all seven areas, every name invented
Between two and eight bays per spot
Prices between 2000 and 6000 paise per hour
No real business is named anywhere in the seed

stories.title: Money helpers with the rounding rule
stories.basis: Small functions, but the rounding rule is a product decision and needs tests at the boundaries.
acceptance: paiseToDisplay renders ₹80 for 8000 and ₹80.50 for 8050
billableHours rounds part hours UP per ADR-003
Tests cover 60 minutes, 90 minutes, and exactly 120 minutes
No float arithmetic anywhere in the money path

stories.title: Concurrency test: two racers, one winner
stories.basis: The test that proves the product's promise. Needs real concurrent connections, not mocks.
acceptance: A test fires N concurrent overlapping booking inserts against a real Postgres
Exactly one succeeds; the rest fail with the exclusion violation
The test fails if the constraint is removed
It runs in CI without Docker

stories.title: GET /api/areas per the contract
stories.basis: One query, one shape, already specified in openapi.yaml.
acceptance: Response matches the Area schema in design/openapi.yaml exactly
A contract test asserts the shape

stories.title: GET /api/availability — derived, single query
stories.basis: The hardest query in the product: bays free for the WHOLE window, grouped to spots, with free-bay counts.
acceptance: Returns only spots with at least one bay free for the entire window
A bay booked 10:00-12:00 is returned as free for a 12:00-14:00 window (half-open ranges)
Cancelled bookings do not block availability
400 on a malformed window or unknown area
An empty result is a 200 with an empty array, never an error
Writes a search_events row including result_count

stories.title: S1 home — area chips, window picker
stories.basis: Mockups exist; this is implementation plus the four states.
acceptance: Matches design/mockups/index.html S1
Duration chips, not an end-time picker
Client-side validation blocks past windows and windows over 12 hours
All four states behave
Keyboard operable end to end, visible focus

stories.title: S2 results — list, map, empty state
stories.basis: Leaflet integration plus five states including the degraded map case.
acceptance: Real spots from the API, with price and free-bay count
Leaflet map with a pin per spot, OSM tiles, no API key
Map failure leaves the list fully usable
Empty state offers 'another area' and 'another time' as controls
Cold-start note appears after ~3s of waiting

stories.title: POST /api/bookings — server-computed price, 409 on race
stories.basis: The endpoint carrying the guarantee. Error translation is the fiddly part.
acceptance: Price is computed server-side; an amount in the request body is ignored
Reference code is CSPRNG, 10 chars Crockford base32, unique
Exclusion violation returns 409 with error code bay_unavailable, never 500
Window outside the spot's opening hours returns 422
A test asserts a posted amount_paise of 0 does not change the charge

stories.title: S3 book — bay chooser, details, price summary
stories.basis: Form plus the 409 recovery path, which returns to a re-run search rather than a stale list.
acceptance: Bay labels shown and selectable
Price summary states the round-up rule on screen
409 shows the real message and returns to a re-run search
Double submit is prevented
Form contents survive an error

stories.title: S4 pay (simulated) + S5 confirmation
stories.basis: Two screens, one state transition, plus the standing demo banner.
acceptance: A payments row is created and the booking becomes confirmed
The demo banner is present and not dismissible on every state of S4
S5 shows the reference code as the largest element, monospace, grouped, copyable
Repeat pay forwards to S5 rather than erroring

stories.title: S6 lookup + arrival, with enumeration controls
stories.basis: Simple screens; the security behaviour is what needs care and tests.
acceptance: A wrong code and an unknown code return identical responses
Rate limited, returning 429 with a usable message
Marking arrival twice is idempotent from the driver's view
arrived_at is set, feeding the north-star metric

stories.title: End-to-end test through the real flow, no mocks
stories.basis: Playwright against a running app and a real database. This is the phase 6 exit condition.
acceptance: One Playwright run: pick area, search, choose bay, book, pay, see code, look it up, mark arrival
Runs against real Postgres with no mocked HTTP or database
Fails if any step regresses

totals.$comment: 24.5 verification-hours against roughly two and a half days, alongside the long-session protocol, hardening, deploy, demo and the field report. This is over-committed and known to be: plan/sequence.md names what gets dropped first if it has to give.
